title: SUM-PAINT Spatial Proteomic Imaging of Neuronal Architecture in Rat Hippocampal Neurons
author: Unterauer, Schentarra, et al.

steps.title: Optional glia feeder preparation
steps.instruction: Prepare glial feeder cells 1–3 weeks before neuron plating (≈2 days total).

substeps.instruction: Grow glial cells in T75 flasks.
Extract cortices from six P0‑P1 pups in dissection solution.
Cut cortices into small pieces with a scalpel.
Transfer tissue to a small Falcon tube with 8 mL dissection solution; invert 10× and let pieces sediment.
Repeat wash four times with 8 mL fresh dissection solution, discarding floating debris each time.
Add pre‑warmed DNase I and Trypsin solutions to the tube, invert gently and rotate 15 min at 37 °C.
Allow tissue to pellet, remove most supernatant leaving a small volume.
Wash pellet four times with 8 mL glial medium, carefully removing supernatant each wash.
Resuspend the final wash by pipetting against the tube wall to homogenize the pellet.
Pass the suspension through a 100 µm cell strainer into a 50 mL Falcon tube and centrifuge 800 rpm (150 g) for 10 min.
Remove supernatant, resuspend cells in 9 mL glial medium without creating bubbles.
Plate cells in three T75 flasks, adding 17 mL glial medium per flask.
Next day, gently tap flasks to detach microglia and fully replace 20 mL glial medium per flask.

steps.title: Coverslip cleaning and coating
steps.instruction: Clean, sterilize, and coat 18 mm #1.5 coverslips for neuron plating.

substeps.instruction: Incubate coverslips in concentrated nitric acid for 24 h in ceramic racks (handle in fume hood).
Wash coverslips 5 × with deionized water (≥5 min each wash).
Autoclave at 121 °C for 30 min.
For sandwich cultures, melt paraffin and place four small paraffin dots on each coverslip using a glass Pasteur pipette.
Incubate coverslips overnight (~16 h) at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ in 1 mg/mL poly‑L‑lysine (PLL) prepared in borate buffer.
Remove PLL solution, transfer coverslips to a 12‑well plate and wash 3 × (≥5 min each) with sterile double‑distilled water.
Aspirate residual water without allowing the coverslips to air‑dry.
Add 1 mL neuron plating medium to each well on the day of primary neuron plating.
Note: Dried PLL‑coated coverslips can be stored sealed with parafilm at 4 °C for up to 1 week.

steps.title: Primary hippocampal neuron isolation
steps.instruction: Dissect, enzymatically digest, and plate hippocampal neurons from E18 or P0‑P2 pups.

substeps.instruction: Decapitate E18 or P0‑P2 pups; immobilize head with thin straight forceps.
Cut skin and skull along the sagittal suture, open skull with scissors and bent forceps, and remove brain into precooled HBSS.
Under a microscope, remove meninges, bisect the brain, and isolate hippocampi using bent forceps.
Collect hippocampi in a dish with precooled HBSS.
Chop hippocampi into ~1 mm pieces with a razor blade.
Transfer pieces to a 15 mL Falcon tube containing 10 mL cold HBSS; let larger pieces settle and discard supernatant.
Add 10 mL pre‑warmed enzymatic solution, gently rotate 60 min at 37 °C.
Pellet tissue, discard enzymatic solution, add 5 mL pre‑warmed inactivation solution, incubate 5 min at 37 °C.
Pellet again, add 10 mL plating medium, let settle, discard medium, add 3 mL plating medium and homogenize by pipetting 10 × (avoid bubbles).
Filter the suspension through a 100 µm cell strainer into a 50 mL Falcon tube; wash strainer with 10 mL plating medium.
Centrifuge 800 rpm (150 g) for 9 min; leave 1.5 mL supernatant, add 5 mL fresh plating medium and resuspend pellet.
Count cells (e.g., Neubauer chamber).
Seed cells on PLL‑coated coverslips at 5 × 10⁴ cells/well for sandwich cultures or 8 × 10⁴ cells/well for mixed cultures.
For mixed cultures, replace plating medium with Neurobasal‑A after 1–2 h; for sandwich cultures, flip coverslips 3–4 h after plating so neurons face the glial feeder layer.
Replace 1/5 of the medium twice weekly with fresh N2‑culture medium; keep incubator openings minimal to limit evaporation.
For mixed cultures, add 10 µL of 8.1 mM 2′‑deoxy‑5‑fluorodeoxyuridine stock per well on the day of plating to inhibit glial proliferation.
Maintain neurons until the desired DIV (e.g., 14–22 DIV).

steps.title: Assemble custom imaging chamber
steps.instruction: Mount the neuron‑seeded coverslip into a custom 18 mm sample chamber and seal with picodent glue.

substeps.instruction: Using fine tweezers, place the coverslip (neurons facing up) onto the chamber holder.
Add 10 µL 1× PBS on top to keep the coverslip humid.
Prepare 1:1 picodent glue (two‑component) and mix thoroughly.
Dispense mixed glue around the outer edge of the chamber with a 10 µL pipette tip; gently press the coverslip down (cells facing downward).
Allow glue to set for up to 10 min, then add 1× PBS to fill the chamber.

steps.title: Permeabilization and blocking
steps.instruction: Incubate the sample with combined permeabilization/blocking buffer.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate PBS from the chamber.
Add 300 µL combined permeabilization/blocking buffer (contains 0.25 % Triton X‑100, 3 % BSA, 0.05 mg/mL salmon sperm DNA) to cover the sample.
Incubate 45 min at room temperature (~21 °C).

steps.title: Gold nanoparticle labeling
steps.instruction: Label the sample with diluted gold nanoparticles for drift correction.

substeps.instruction: Wash the sample 3 × with 1× PBS.
Add gold nanoparticles diluted 1:3 in PBS; incubate 5 min at room temperature (~21 °C).
Wash 3 × with 1× PBS.

steps.title: Prepare primary‑antibody / nanobody mixes
steps.instruction: Create incubation mixes for the first barcoding round (six targets).

substeps.instruction: For each target, pipette 10 µL antibody incubation buffer into a 0.5 mL tube (six tubes total).
Add the appropriate primary antibody to achieve the published dilution (e.g., Bassoon 1:200 → 1.5 µL primary Ab).
Add the corresponding secondary nanobody (barcode) to the same final dilution (e.g., 1:200 → 1.5 µL).
Mix gently (flick tube) and briefly centrifuge.
Incubate each tube ≥1 h at room temperature (~21 °C) or overnight at 4 °C.
Prepare blocking nanobody stock: mix 1 µL of 30 µM stock with 9 µL 1× PBS (final 3 µM).
Add 1 µL of the appropriate blocking nanobody to each primary/secondary tube; incubate 5 min at room temperature.
Prepare the final incubation mix: combine 200 µL antibody incubation buffer with 0.5 µL of each species‑specific blocking nanobody stock (30 µM).
Pool the volumes from the six pre‑incubated tubes into the final mix.

steps.title: Primary antibody incubation on sample
steps.instruction: Apply the pooled primary‑antibody/secondary‑nanobody mix to the sample.

substeps.instruction: Wash the sample once with 1× PBS.
Add the final incubation mix to fully cover the sample.
Incubate 90 min at room temperature (~21 °C).

steps.title: Post‑primary washes
steps.instruction: Wash the sample to remove unbound antibodies.

substeps.instruction: Wash 4 × with 1× PBS.
Wash once with Buffer Cw.
Wash once with 2× SSC.

steps.title: Prepare secondary‑label mix
steps.instruction: Make the hybridization mix containing fluorophore‑labeled docking strands.

substeps.instruction: Pipette 1 mL optimized hybridization buffer (contains 10 % dextran sulfate) into a 1.5 mL tube.
Add 1 µL of each secondary‑label stock (100 µM) to reach 100 nM per label; for six labels the total concentration is 600 nM.
Mix gently after each addition to avoid bubbles.

steps.title: Secondary label incubation
steps.instruction: Hybridize the secondary‑label strands to the bound nanobodies.

substeps.instruction: Add the secondary‑label mix to the sample.
Incubate 15 min at room temperature (~21 °C).

steps.title: Final washes before imaging
steps.instruction: Wash the sample to remove excess secondary labels.

substeps.instruction: Wash 5 × with 2× SSC.
Wash once with Buffer Cw.
Proceed to SUM‑PAINT imaging within 30 min.

steps.title: Synapse segmentation in Picasso
steps.instruction: Select synaptic regions using Picasso:Render and export localizations.

substeps.instruction: Open Picasso:Render and load all protein channels.
Activate the “Pick” tool, set Pick size to 10 (≈1.3 µm).
Interactively pick synapses based on colocalization of scaffold and vesicle‑pool markers.
Save pick regions (File → Save Pick Regions) to generate a YAML file.
Load all protein channels to be analyzed.
Load the saved pick coordinates (File → Load Pick Regions).
Export localizations for the picked areas (Save picked localizations → apply to all channels sequentially).

steps.title: DBSCAN clustering of synapse localizations
steps.instruction: Cluster synaptic localizations to separate signal from background.

substeps.instruction: Load a synaptic marker channel (e.g., Synapsin) in Picasso:Render.
Open Postprocessing → Clustering → DBSCAN.
Set radius to 80 nm and minimum density to 5 localizations; run clustering.
Filter clusters by size using a cutoff determined from random non‑synaptic regions.
Repeat DBSCAN and filtering for each protein channel.

steps.title: Histogram feature extraction
steps.instruction: Compute histogram‑based descriptors for each synapse.

substeps.instruction: Load raw (pre‑DBSCAN) synaptic localizations into the analysis script.
Calculate the synapse centre as the arithmetic mean of x, y, z coordinates.
Generate a histogram within a 10‑pixel diameter (≈pick size) using 20 bins, centred on the synapse centre.
Derive histogram features: mean, standard deviation, skewness, kurtosis, entropy, intensity minimum and maximum.
Calculate histogram distances between protein pairs: Wasserstein, Jensen‑Shannon, Cosine, and pairwise maximum distance.

steps.title: Clustering feature extraction
steps.instruction: Derive quantitative descriptors from DBSCAN‑filtered clusters.

substeps.instruction: Load DBSCAN‑filtered localizations into the analysis script.
Compute centre of mass for all localizations of each protein.
Compute centre of mass for DBSCAN‑filtered localizations of each protein.
Calculate clustering features: total localisation count (pre‑filter), largest cluster size (post‑filter), standard deviation (pre‑filter), convex hull volume, pairwise volume ratios.
Calculate cluster‑distance features: pairwise centre‑of‑mass distances between proteins and distance from each protein to the overall synaptic centre of mass.
Compute alphashape features: alphashape volume, localisation density (localisations per volume), and surface area.

steps.title: Compile feature matrix
steps.instruction: Combine all extracted features into a single table for downstream analysis.

substeps.instruction: Merge histogram, clustering, and alphashape features for each synapse.
Export the combined matrix as a CSV (or other preferred format).
Replace any NaN values with 0 or another defined placeholder.

steps.title: UMAP dimensionality reduction
steps.instruction: Reduce the feature space to two dimensions for visualization.

substeps.instruction: Remove features with zero variance across all synapses.
Apply Z‑score normalisation to each remaining feature.
Create a UMAP model with n_components = 2 (set random_state for reproducibility).
Generate the 2‑D embedding and plot as a scatterplot.
Optionally adjust min_dist (default 0.1) or random_state to improve visual separation.

steps.title: Cluster UMAP embedding
steps.instruction: Identify synaptic subpopulations in the UMAP space.

substeps.instruction: Run K‑means clustering on the UMAP coordinates for a range of cluster numbers.
Calculate silhouette_score for each clustering result.
Select the cluster number with the highest silhouette score (or use elbow method as confirmation).
Assign cluster labels to each synapse for downstream biological interpretation.

steps.title: Quality control of localization data
steps.instruction: Filter out low‑quality datasets before analysis.

substeps.instruction: Exclude any sample with average localisation precision > 8 nm (except Lifeact experiments).
Discard datasets with secondary‑label extinction < 99.5 % or with signal deviating markedly from single‑target DNA‑PAINT controls.

description: In this protocol, we describe the details of obtaining neuronal architecture maps using SUM-PAINT super-resolution imaging. This technology was used to generate a 30 plex neuronal atlas in Unterauer et al.1 with the specific purpose of understanding the heterogeneity of synapses. It should be noted that SUM-PAINT multiplexing is not limited to neuronal imaging but can be applied to any target system of interest. Fluorescence imaging methods depend on available affinity reagents and before starting with SUM-PAINT, all affinity reagents (e.g., primary antibodies) need to be thoroughly tested in standard fluorescence microscopy. We will outline how to continue with troubleshooting these reagents, first for classical DNA-PAINT imaging and second for the assembly of multiplexing “codebooks” for SUM-PAINT. Following this assembly procedure, the codebooks in Unterauer et al.1 can be extended or modified to suit different application scenarios. We developed a comprehensive workflow from image acquisition to the analysis of morphometric features of synaptic structures.
